title: THE WRONG WORLD
show_concept: Jim accidentally uses a Glitched World Lock on his phone and pulls a living Growtopia Default Skin into the real world. The visitor is frightened, displaced, and certain that his pixel world was already real. Jim becomes his guide through ordinary human life while they search for a way home. Neither notices that the same open phone portal has allowed a Demonic Growtopian to begin crossing into Jim's empty bedroom. The series balances dramatic portal mystery and escalating danger with the Default Skin applying Growtopia rules to real-world objects, buildings, money, doors, and ownership.
style_tags: dual-realm animated cinematic series. Growtopia and phone-portal imagery uses crisp illustrated 2D pixel art in a bright pseudo-isometric 2.5D diorama, blocky pixelated proportions, thick clean black outlines, cheerful cyan green and gold palette, coherent three-quarter projection, and layered tile platforms, no Minecraft and no voxel CGI. Real-world scenes transform into high-end stylized 3D animated-feature visuals with appealing rounded adult proportions, expressive eyes and brows, detailed soft skin and fabric, warm practical apartment lighting, cinematic depth of field, polished global illumination, emotionally readable faces, and grounded physical environments. Characters crossing the portal visibly transition from flat pixel sprites into expressive stylized 3D human or humanoid forms while preserving exact canonical Growtopia costume colors, silhouette, props, and moral identity.

cta.text_note: Use the approved existing Growtopia CTA as-is. Do not generate replacement lettering.

production_rules: Maximum 6 scenes and $7 total generation cost per episode.
Every episode begins with a spoken conflict hook, followed by the separate text title-card interstitial.
Every episode ends on a dramatic cliffhanger before the locked Growtopia CTA.
All scene clips use Kling v3 Standard I2V, including dialogue. Kling Avatar is forbidden.
Dialogue uses Kling native audio with generate_audio:true, shot_type:customize, multi_prompt, and no more than 2 voice_ids per request.
Voice samples are series-owned. Initial voice directions are locked here; permanent voice URLs remain null until the Debug-mode Sound phase is explicitly approved and generates them.
Do not use character names in NB2 or Kling visual prompts. Use the exact state-appropriate prompt_descriptor and the matching owned reference image.
Generate fresh series-owned character references. Do not reuse character refs from another Growtopia format automatically.
Do not attach separate Kling Elements by default. Animate the approved complete scene PNG directly.
Real-world Default Skin must retain canonical tan skin, bright cyan/turquoise shirt, medium-blue pants, and white sneakers in every scene.
In-game Default Skin must retain canonical tan blocky skin, bright cyan/turquoise shirt, and medium-blue pants.
Demonic Growtopian must retain dark red skin, black horns, black bat wings, glowing red eyes, and a dark smoky aura in both pixel and real-world states.
Portal transitions use restrained square pixel particles and colored light. Do not reconstruct or rotate bodies during animation.
The real world is stylized cinematic 3D feature animation, not photoreal live action. Preserve adult proportions and emotional facial acting without toy-like anatomy or oversized chibi heads.
When a character materializes, the generated start frame already shows the character landed or mostly formed; Kling performs only small settling motion and fading particles.
For the EP1 cliffhanger, the generated start frame already contains part of the Demonic red claw emerging from the phone. Kling only extends the hand slightly and grips the bedspread.
Do not rely on readable phone UI. The Glitched World Lock and portal meaning must be conveyed through dialogue, acting, color, and physical props.
Keep EP1 production inside Jim's bedroom, apartment window area, and immediate hallway so the real-world introduction feels intimate and continuous.
Background music is mandatory and must be generated with MiniMax Music.
Clamp every subtitle event to its dialogue scene window. No subtitle may overlap action scenes, the title interstitial, cliffhanger silence, or CTA.

episode_summaries.title: Press Undo
episode_summaries.summary: Jim taps Use on the Glitched World Lock; the phone briefly shows real Growtopia gameplay before Default materializes in his bedroom, already mid-panic. Jim and Default are both simultaneously stunned — Default at the huge ordinary room, Jim at a stranger appearing in it — before Jim realizes it's tied to the lock. A beat of dark physical comedy (Default nearly swats a lamp, thinking it's a farmable block) gives way to Jim deciding they need to hide Default and find a way to send him home; they leave the bedroom together. Left empty, the still-glowing phone lets a Monster Nian claw and forearm push into the room.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: A Monster Nian claw and forearm emerge from the phone, human-scaled, in the empty bedroom.
episode_summaries.notes: Jim locked at 14-15 years old (teenage, not young adult) and the EP1 antagonist locked as Monster Nian (canonical Growtopia mob, no wings) per explicit user override of the original Demonic-season-arc plan for this cliffhanger specifically.

planned_arc.note: Season 1 follows Jim and Default trying to reopen the portal while Demonic learns how Growtopia ownership rules can corrupt the real world. Fish-out-of-water comedy grows from Default treating ordinary life literally, but every episode advances the portal mystery and threat.

episodes.title: Press Undo
episodes.summary: Jim taps Use on the Glitched World Lock and sees real Growtopia gameplay on his phone before Default materializes in his bedroom, already panicking. Jim and Default are both simultaneously stunned; a physical gag with a lamp leads into Jim's decision to hide Default and search for a way home. They leave the bedroom together. Left alone, a Monster Nian claw and forearm emerge from the still-glowing phone.
episodes.cliffhanger: In the empty bedroom, a Monster Nian claw and forearm emerge from the phone, human-scaled.

episodes.title: Outside
episodes.summary: Jim introduces Default to traffic, shops, food, money, and the rule that real buildings cannot be broken for blocks. Default is overwhelmed but fascinated. Back at the apartment, unseen red pixel traces spread from the bedroom.
episodes.cliffhanger: Jim's ordinary front-door lock has been replaced by a glowing World Lock from the inside.

episodes.title: World Locked
episodes.summary: Jim and Default discover that the apartment has become a locked world. Neighbors cannot enter or leave. Default recognizes the work as deliberate and admits that someone hostile may have followed him.
episodes.cliffhanger: A calm demonic voice speaks through every locked door: 'Owner online.'

episodes.title: Real Inventory
episodes.summary: Default learns that touching portal-corrupted objects can pull them into a temporary real-world inventory. Jim sees a possible way to recover the Glitched World Lock, but Demonic steals a key object first.
episodes.cliffhanger: Jim reaches into the inventory glow and pulls out an object that belonged to Default's world.

episodes.title: The Trade
episodes.summary: Demonic finally approaches Jim directly and offers to reopen the portal in exchange for ownership of one real-world room. Default calls it an obvious scam, but the offer includes proof that his world still exists.
episodes.cliffhanger: Jim accepts the trade without telling Default.

episodes.title: One Room
episodes.summary: The traded room becomes a small Growtopia biome inside the apartment. Default feels at home for the first time, while Jim realizes Demonic can expand the conversion through connected doors.
episodes.cliffhanger: A second real apartment begins pixelating through the shared wall.

episodes.title: The Wizard
episodes.summary: Jim and Default force open a tiny stable portal and pull through a Legendary Wizard who knows the Glitched World Lock's origin. His arrival adds comic chaos but confirms that the two realities are collapsing together.
episodes.cliffhanger: The Wizard reveals that Default was not selected randomly.

episodes.title: Not an NPC
episodes.summary: Default learns that Jim initially believed he was only game code. Their trust breaks just as Demonic offers Default a guaranteed path home. Jim must prove that he now believes Default's world is genuinely alive.
episodes.cliffhanger: Default walks through Demonic's portal alone.

episodes.title: Unlocked
episodes.summary: Jim and the Wizard follow Default into the unstable border between worlds. They discover that Demonic needs a willing Growtopian to place the final lock on reality.
episodes.cliffhanger: Default raises the Glitched World Lock over the real city.

episodes.title: The Wrong World
episodes.summary: Default rejects Demonic's deal and helps Jim break the first real-world lock. The portal stabilizes long enough to choose between home and his new friendship, but the broken lock has already opened routes for other characters.
episodes.cliffhanger: After the portal closes, a cheerful unfamiliar voice speaks from Jim's phone: 'You buying or selling?'
